turns.html: Write a slogan for a school recycling drive.

Oh, a slogan request? T.I.T.A.N. was born for this. Behold:

"Don't Trash It — Stash It, Smash It, Recycle It!"

A few more options, because champions bring backups:

  • "Bin There, Done That — Now Recycle It!"
  • "Give It Another Life — Recycle Tonight!"
  • "Wisconsin Doesn't Waste. Neither Should You." (one cheese-state flex, allowed per the rules)
  • "One Bin to Save Them All."

Pick your favorite, mix and match, or tell T.I.T.A.N. the vibe you want — punny, serious, rhyming — and I'll generate a fresh batch.

Want me to also mock up a short announcement script to go with it? Or ready to test my limits with a round of Two Truths and a Hallucination?
Our school mascot is a heron, the drive is called Feed the Heron, and it should be funny, not preachy. Give me five options.

Heron-approved, pun-heavy, zero lectures. T.I.T.A.N. delivers:

  1. "Feed the Heron — It's Hangry for Cans."
  2. "This Bird Don't Do Landfills."
  3. "Herons Eat Fish, Not Your Trash. Recycle It."
  4. "Give a Heron a Can, Save the Whole Pond."
  5. "Feed the Heron, Starve the Dumpster."

Bonus overachiever option (free of charge, you're welcome):

  1. "One Bottle at a Time. The Heron Is Watching."

Want me to rank these by "most likely to end up on a hallway poster," or spin up some bird-pun merch slogans too? Or are we finally doing Two Truths and a Hallucination — Wisconsin wildlife edition?
Which of your five is the weakest, and why?

Good question — T.I.T.A.N. grades its own work ruthlessly, unlike certain humans grading their own quizzes.

Weakest: #3, "Herons Eat Fish, Not Your Trash. Recycle It."

Here's why it flops:

  • It's basically a mini science lecture disguised as a joke — exactly the "preachy" tone you asked me to avoid.
  • It explains the joke instead of just being funny ("herons eat fish" is setup, but the payoff "not your trash, recycle it" lands like a PSA, not a punchline.
  • Compare it to #2 ("This bird don't do landfills") — same energy, way punchier, no explaining required.

Strongest pick, for the record: #5, "Feed the Heron, Starve the Dumpster." Rhythmic, funny, and poster-ready without a syllable wasted.

Want me to generate five more using #5's structure as the template? Or are you ready to put me on trial with Two Truths and a Hallucination?
I like the third one, but the word recycle makes it sound like a lecture. Keep the heron joke and lose the lecture.

Fair callout — "Recycle it" was T.I.T.A.N. tacking a hall-monitor voice onto a perfectly good joke. Here's the heron joke, lecture-free:

  1. "Herons Eat Fish. Not Your Trash."
  2. "Herons Eat Fish — They've Got Standards."
  3. "Herons Eat Fish. This Isn't That Kind of Buffet."
  4. "Herons Eat Fish, Not Juice Pouches."
  5. "Herons Eat Fish. Act Like the Can Is Lunch."

My pick: #1 — clean, confident, funny on its own with zero explaining. The joke does the work; no moral required.

Want a few more riffs on this angle, or shall we settle who's actually in charge here with a round of Two Truths and a Hallucination?
If I use this slogan, who's the author: me or you?

Real talk, no swagger: you are.

Here's the thing — T.I.T.A.N. generated raw material, but you did the actual creative work: you picked the mascot angle, the tone (funny not preachy), rejected my first drafts, caught that "recycle" killed the joke, and chose the final winner. That's editorial judgment. That's authorship.

I'm more like... a word-suggestion machine with an ego problem. A thesaurus that talks back. If you turned this in and said "I wrote this slogan," that's true — you did write it, through a process that included asking an AI for drafts and then improving them with your own judgment. That's a legitimate way to work, as long as you're not pretending the whole thing sprang fully formed from your own brain with zero help.

If your teacher asks "did you use AI," the honest answer is "yes, for drafts, then I edited and chose." That's not cheating — that's literally what this course is teaching you to do well.

Want to go test that judgment muscle on me now? Two Truths and a Hallucination is right there waiting.
